message.content: In lions, the most well‑documented dominant genetic trait is the **presence of a mane in males**. The gene that drives mane development is inherited in a dominant fashion: a single copy of the allele is enough for a male lion to grow a mane, while females (who are homozygous for the recessive allele) do not develop one. This dominant trait is what gives male lions their iconic, mane‑covered appearance.
